draft.title: Longships and the Viking homeland
card: The Vikings came from Scandinavia, the region that is now Norway, Sweden and Denmark. Much of the land was mountain, forest or cold, so good farmland was scarce.
Scarce farmland meant many families struggled to feed themselves. Looking for wealth, land and trade overseas was one way to deal with this.
Viking longships were light and fast. They were built with overlapping planks, so they could be flexible and quick on the open sea.
Longships had a shallow hull, so they could cross oceans and also sail up shallow rivers. This let Vikings reach places far from the coast.
draft.remember: Little farmland pushed Vikings to look overseas, and longships took them across seas and up rivers.

a.q: Why were Viking longships useful for reaching places far inland?
opts: Their shallow hulls let them sail up shallow rivers
Their heavy hulls let them carry huge armies over land
Their deep hulls let them sail only in the open ocean
Their large size let them block rivers to stop other ships
a.why: A shallow hull sits high in the water, so a longship could travel up rivers that deeper ships could not enter. The tempting option about heavy hulls is wrong because longships were light, not heavy.
a.clue: Think about how deep the hull sat in the water.

b.q: Sigrid's family lives in Norway in the 800s. Their small farm cannot grow enough food for everyone. Which fact about the homeland best explains why some Vikings looked overseas?
opts: Scandinavia had little good farmland
Scandinavia had no forests to build houses
Scandinavia had no coast for ships to sail from
Scandinavia had too many rivers to cross by boat
b.why: Mountains, forest and cold left little land for farming, so families looked overseas for wealth, land and trade. The option about having no coast is wrong because Scandinavia had a long coast, which is where longships sailed from.
b.clue: Think about what the family needed to grow food.

a.best: Their shallow hulls let them sail up shallow rivers

problems.detail: The stem already says the family's small farm cannot grow enough food, and the clue points again to growing food. Together they almost restate the right option. The other options are also clearly false from the card (Scandinavia had a coast and forests), so a student can pick the answer without understanding the idea.

b.q: Sigrid's family lives in Norway in the 800s. Which pairing best explains why Vikings like them could travel so far?
opts: Scarce farmland gave a reason, and longships a way to go
Rich farmland gave a reason, and longships a way to go

Longships gave a reason, and scarce farmland a way to go
